assignments.title: Primary Source Report: Gandhi and the Declaration of Israel
assignments.html:
PRIMARY SOURCE REPORT
Gandhi and the Declaration of Israel
Decolonization and Israel
16 points · text entry
❋ ✦ ❋
Before you start

Finish both lessons and read both sources first. Your notes from each page are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the page, so open it before you write. Then write your answers and submit them in this assignment.

QUESTIONS
1. Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in 1909, long before India was free. The Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel was read on May 14, 1948. For each document, say who is speaking, who the audience is, and what the speaker wanted to achieve. How might it matter that one was written before independence and the other on the day a state was proclaimed?
2. Choose one passage from Hind Swaraj. Quote it in a few words, then explain in your own words what Gandhi says that self-rule requires of Indians themselves, and not only of the British.
3. The Declaration of Israel gives reasons for the new state. Choose one of the reasons it gives. Quote it in a few words and explain it. Then use the lesson “Palestine, Israel, and the Arab World” to say how a Palestinian Arab reading the same document in 1948 might respond, and why.
4. Each document speaks for a people and leaves out some voices. Name one voice that is missing from each document, using what you learned in both lessons. Then say what a historian should look at in order to hear that voice.
GRADING RUBRIC (16 pts)
Criteria Excellent (4) Proficient (3) Developing (2) Beginning (1)
Understanding of the material
4 pts		 Reads both sources accurately and draws on specific details from each, along with what the week's lessons taught. Reads both sources accurately but uses few specific details, or leans on only one. Shows partial understanding of one or both sources, with some errors or vague claims. Misreads the sources or does not refer to them.
Quality of reasoning
4 pts		 Connects each claim to evidence and compares the sources with care. Explains why a speaker's purpose, position, and moment matter. Supports most claims with evidence. The comparison is sound but not fully developed. States conclusions with little support, or describes the sources without comparing them. Offers opinions without evidence from the sources.
Clarity and precision of expression
4 pts		 Writes in clear, well-organized sentences. Quotations are short, accurate, and introduced. Treats each people's account with fairness. Writing is clear with minor lapses in organization or precision. Writing is often unclear or disorganized, and quotations are unclear or misplaced. Writing is too unclear to follow.
Intellectual honesty
4 pts		 Names the limits of what each source can show and says what remains uncertain without overclaiming. Acknowledges at least one limit of the evidence. Mentions limits only in passing, or claims more than the sources allow. Treats each source as complete and beyond question.
Total:
16 pts total
SUBMISSION

Answer all four questions in complete sentences. Submit your answers in the text box on the Canvas assignment page. Aim for one solid paragraph for each question. You do not need an outside source. Your teacher will read your work and return a rubric score with a short comment.

quizzes.title: Module Intro: Decolonization and Israel
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRO
Decolonization and Israel
2 questions · survey · one attempt
❋ ✦ ❋
Essential question for this week
Why could the European empires not be held after World War II, and what followed in India and in Palestine?
Instructions

Welcome to Decolonization and Israel. This short check-in is not graded. Your answers help your teacher see where each student is starting, so answer honestly.

What you will be able to do

The Empires Let Go: India, Africa, Asia

  • Explain why European empires in Asia and Africa could not be held after World War II.
  • Describe how India won independence and why it was partitioned.
  • Compare the paths to independence taken in India, Vietnam, Algeria, and Ghana.

Palestine, Israel, and the Arab World

  • Describe the origins of Zionism and the competing promises made about Palestine during World War I.
  • Explain how the partition plan of 1947 and the war of 1948 created Israel and a refugee crisis.
  • Summarize the major wars and peace efforts between Israel and its neighbors through the 1990s.

discussions.title: Discussion: Partition: Could India Have Stayed United?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Partition: Could India Have Stayed United?
Decolonization and Israel
10 points · threaded discussion
❋ ✦ ❋
Before you start

Finish both lessons first. Your notes from each lesson are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the lesson, so open it before you post. Then post your answer here and reply to one classmate.

DISCUSSION PROMPT

About one in four Indians was Muslim, and many Muslims feared being a permanent minority in a state ruled by a Hindu majority. Jinnah demanded a separate homeland. Gandhi and Nehru opposed dividing the country. Britain decided to leave, set an early date, and gave a lawyer who had never seen India a few weeks to draw the borders. The partition set off one of the largest migrations in history, and hundreds of thousands died.

Take a position. Could India have stayed united? Support your position with at least two specific details from the lessons, and include one detail that points the other way. Explain why you weigh the evidence as you do.

Aim for about 150 to 200 words.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a detail from the lessons that they did not use. If not, explain respectfully where it falls short, and point to a detail from the lessons that supports your view.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
Criteria Substantive (full credit) Thin (partial credit) Missing (no credit)
Claim and evidence
5 pts		 Takes a clear position, supports it with at least two specific details from the lessons, and deals fairly with a detail that points the other way. Takes a position but gives only one detail, or stays general, or ignores the opposing detail. No post, or no clear position.
Response to a classmate
5 pts		 Answers a specific point in a classmate's post and either strengthens it with a new detail or explains politely where it falls short. Replies in general terms, such as agreeing or disagreeing without a detail from the lessons. No reply.
10 pts total
